idea-plugin.name: Aegis Debug
idea-plugin.description:
Aegis Debug — privacy-first debugging for IntelliJ

Static-first analysis. Deterministic fixes. Optional local or cloud AI.

Aegis Debug finds real bugs in your TypeScript and JavaScript code without sending anything to the cloud by default. Every finding is labeled with its source — engine-verified, local AI, or cloud AI — so you always know what you are trusting.

What's inside

  • Language Support — Full static analysis and fixers for TypeScript & JavaScript; project graph and cycle detection for Kotlin & Java.
  • Eleven deterministic analyzers — syntax, compilation, null safety (TS/JS/Kotlin), state-before-init, async flow, circular dependencies, complexity, unsafe-cast (Kotlin), type-mismatch (Kotlin), redundant-let (Kotlin).
  • Five deterministic fixers with diff preview and native undo.
  • NeuroMap — visual project graph with per-file issue overlay.
  • Engine status pill — know at a glance whether you're on static, local AI, or cloud AI.
  • Ollama (local) or OpenAI (cloud) — both optional, both off by default.
  • Secure key storage via IntelliJ PasswordSafe.

Privacy by default

  • No telemetry.
  • No cloud uploads unless you configure them explicitly.
  • Local mode works offline.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.0.0-alpha.1 — First V2 milestone: dynamic validation foundation

  • Runtime-confirmed provenance tier. A fourth source tag, RUNTIME_CONFIRMED, joins STATIC / AI_LOCAL / AI_CLOUD. Findings promoted to this tier get a distinct pulsing badge and outrank unconfirmed siblings in the issue list.
  • Debug-session cross-check (null-safety). When the debugger pauses on a line carrying a null-safety finding, Aegis evaluates the relevant variable in the current frame: if the value is actually null/undefined, the finding is promoted to RUNTIME_CONFIRMED with confidence 1.0; if it's non-null, the finding is demoted with confidence 0.1.
  • Confidence pill. Each finding now shows a CONFIRMED / LIKELY / UNCONFIRMED chip derived from the runtime tier and confidence score, surfacing trust at a glance.
  • Quick-fix intention actions. The deterministic fixers are now exposed as native IntentionAction entries; press Alt+Enter on a flagged line to apply the same fix the detail panel offers, with full undo support.
  • Internal: sendCurrentDebugFrame now rethrows ProcessCanceledException per the project's PCE-handling convention.
  • Still on the V2 backlog (continuation in 2.0.0-alpha.2 onward): test-suite cross-check, false-positive suppression memory, Python support, native Problems tool window emit, inspection profile integration, streaming AI responses.

1.5.0 — Pre-V2 structural refactor

  • Internal restructure only. No user-visible behavior change. All analyzers, fixers, languages, and UI surfaces are unchanged.
  • The project-level service is split into focused collaborators (analysis orchestrator, UI event router, file-change watcher, debug-session coordinator, report exporter) to clear the path for V2's dynamic-validation features.
  • The two AI services (Ollama, OpenAI) now share a common abstract parent, eliminating ~120 LOC of duplication around caching, prompt dispatch, and HTTP client setup.

1.4.1 — Audit-driven correctness and safety hardening

  • Critical: Cancel during analysis is now honored — a previous catch swallowed the platform's cancellation signal, leaving analyzers running after the user clicked Stop.
  • Security: JCEF event payloads now use proper JSON encoding throughout; eliminates a payload-corruption / JS-injection class in the tool window bridge.
  • Concurrency: The in-memory graph's adjacency lists are now safe under concurrent edge inserts; cycle detection rewritten as iterative DFS removing the recursion-depth ceiling.
  • HTTP: AI HTTP responses are wrapped in use { } — connections return to the OkHttp pool deterministically on JSON-decode failure.
  • NullSafetyFixer: Now PSI-driven; no longer rewrites varName. sequences inside string literals or comments.
  • Settings: maxComplexity threshold for ComplexityAnalyzer surfaced in the UI (default 10, unchanged).
  • Observability: ApiKeyManager logs PasswordSafe failures; AIAnalyzer logs files skipped due to the 2000-line cap.

1.4.0 — Cleanup, report-export rewrite, smart-cast walker (2026-05-09)

  • Report export rewritten on StringBuilder; new file-chooser UX; IDE notification with "Open in browser" / "Show in Files" actions.
  • Smart-cast walker resolves V1.3's three documented known limitations.
  • JVM-language AI prompts include a Function Signatures block.
  • Marketplace copy refreshed (eleven analyzers, five fixers).
  • KaExpressionTypeProvider.getReturnType(KtDeclaration) deprecation resolved.
  • Java regex fallback enrichment for returnType / paramTypes.

1.3.0 — Kotlin K2 + Analysis API (2026-04-29)

  • First-class K2-mode support: minimum IDE raised to 2024.3.
  • Rewrote AEG-NULL-KT-001 on the Kotlin Analysis API for type-aware findings.
  • Added AEG-CAST-KT-001: unsafe as downcasts.
  • Added AEG-TYPE-KT-001: type mismatches between declared types and initializers.
  • Added AEG-REDUNDANT-LET-KT-001: redundant ?.let after smart-cast.
  • Two new deterministic fixers: unsafe-cast and redundant-let.
  • Function symbols now carry rendered returnType and paramTypes for Kotlin and Java.

1.2.0 — Hardening release (2026-04-25)

  • PSI-backed symbol extraction for Kotlin and Java (replacing regex-only paths).
  • New AEG-NULL-KT-001: Kotlin null-safety analyzer (PSI-backed, conservative-miss bias).
  • Resilient AI JSON parsing — three-strategy extractor (direct → fenced → bracket-balanced) with telemetry.
  • Single-source AI fan-out: Ollama and OpenAI both flow through one AIAnalyzer.
  • Few-shot examples in detectIssues and jointFix prompts.
  • Cross-file dependent re-analysis cascade (capped by maxDependentsToReanalyze, default 20).

1.1.0 — Syntax & Compilation Error Detection (2026-04-16)

  • Added AEG-SYNTAX-001: detects parse-level syntax errors across Kotlin, Java, TS, JS.
  • Added AEG-COMPILE-001: surfaces IDE-reported compilation errors (unresolved references, type mismatches).
  • Broken-file skip: downstream static and AI analyzers now skip files with syntax/compilation errors to prevent false positives.
  • Two-phase analysis engine: early (syntax/compile) and late (pattern) passes.

1.0.0 — V1 GA (2026-04-15)

  • Initial public release.
  • Five static analyzers with documented rule IDs.
  • Deterministic fixes with PSI-validity safety check.
  • Ollama and OpenAI backends with fallback-to-static on failure.
  • Cancellable analysis with progress indicator.
